meta.intent: help me draft a proposal to national institute of mental health due by febuary 15 2026
meta.rationale: Securing NIMH funding will enable the proposed mental health research, support personnel and resources, and advance scientific understanding and interventions in a prioritized area of need.

tasks: Gather names of all key personnel and confirm roles/effort for the proposal.
Request NIH biosketch templates and current/pending support forms from each contributor.
Review returned biosketches for format, accuracy, and completeness; request corrections as needed.
Collect institutional signatures or confirmations if required and compile into a single personnel folder.
Create a master checklist tracking which biosketches/current-pending forms are submission-ready.

goal.subgoal.init.assemble_biosketches_c.text: Assemble NIH-format biosketches, current and pending support forms, and required documentation for all key personnel and senior/key staff.

tasks: Populate eRA Commons and Grants.gov forms with accurate project and personnel information.
Upload finalized documents (Specific Aims, Research Strategy, biosketches, budget justification, DMSP, IRB documentation, letters) into the submission portal.
Run final format/attachment checks per FOA instructions and resolve any errors flagged by the submission system.
Obtain final institutional approvals/signatures required for submission and confirm submitter credentials in eRA Commons.
Submit the application to NIMH by the external submission deadline (February 15, 2026) and archive confirmation receipts.

goal.subgoal.init.compile_the_complete_a.text: Compile the complete application package, complete eRA Commons / Grants.gov forms, and submit the proposal to NIMH by the external deadline.

tasks: Assemble a complete draft application and run it against the NIMH/FOA checklist to identify gaps.
Schedule an internal review meeting with co-investigators and institutional reviewers to gather feedback.
Assign revision tasks based on reviewer comments and implement changes to each component.
Confirm that IRB, budget, biosketches, letters, and research documents meet institutional requirements for routing.
Prepare a final package for institutional sign-off by the internal deadline (Feb 8) and for external submission.

goal.subgoal.init.conduct_internal_revie.text: Conduct internal reviews against an NIMH/FOA checklist, iterate revisions, and bring each component to submission-ready quality for institutional routing.

tasks: Create a section outline mapping Significance, Innovation, and Approach to the Specific Aims.
Assign writing tasks for each subsection among designated writers and set internal checkpoints.
Prepare and integrate available preliminary data figures/tables and annotate methods/analyses needing completion.
Draft analytic plans, power/feasibility rationale, and contingency approaches for anticipated challenges.
Revise the Research Strategy to ensure alignment with the Specific Aims and FOA requirements.

goal.subgoal.init.develop_and_complete_t.text: Develop and complete the Research Strategy (Significance, Innovation, Approach), integrating preliminary data and analytic plans.

tasks: Draft a one-page Specific Aims document outlining objectives, hypotheses, and expected impact.
Write a concise scientific abstract and a plain-language lay summary for public use.
Circulate drafts to co-investigators for feedback and incorporate revisions.
Confirm that aims and abstracts conform to FOA page/format limits and update as needed.
Approve a submission-ready version to feed into the Research Strategy and application package.

goal.subgoal.init.draft_and_finalize_the.text: Draft and finalize the Specific Aims page, project abstracts, and a lay summary suitable for the NIMH FOA.

tasks: List required letter writers (collaborators, consultants, institutional officials) and confirm willingness to provide letters.
Provide letter writers with a one-page brief, draft text suggestions, and any FOA-specific language to include.
Set and communicate expected delivery dates (to align with institutional routing/internal review).
Collect letters, review them for required content and signatures, and request revisions if missing elements.
Store finalized letters in the application folder in the required format for upload.

goal.subgoal.init.obtain_and_finalize_le.text: Identify, request, and finalize letters of support, institutional commitment letters, and collaborator/consultant confirmations.

tasks: Draft IRB protocol narrative, recruitment materials, consent forms, and participant-facing documents based on the Research Strategy.
Complete the Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMSP) consistent with NIH/DMSP guidance.
Identify anticipated human-subjects risk level and document protections for privacy/confidentiality.
Confirm IRB application status (pending) and prepare any supporting appendices or referenced study materials.
Coordinate with institutional research compliance office to determine submission steps and required sign-offs.

goal.subgoal.init.prepare_human_subjects.text: Prepare human subjects documentation, IRB application materials, data management and sharing plan, and other required compliance documentation.

tasks: Provide the grants/budget manager (grand manager) with required inputs: proposed personnel effort, key cost items, and any subcontract details.
Collect institutional F&A/indirect cost rates, salary ceilings, and other rate agreements needed for the budget.
Draft a detailed budget justification describing personnel effort, other direct costs, and rationale for major items.
Obtain institutional facilities and resources statements (e.g., core facilities, lab space) for the application.
Review the completed budget for consistency with effort listed on biosketches and with the FOA budget limits.

goal.subgoal.init.prepare_the_budget_det.text: Prepare the budget, detailed budget justification, and institutional facilities/resources documentation in coordination with the institutional grants/budget manager.

extra.1.question: Which NIMH funding mechanism and FOA are you targeting (e.g., R01, R21, K-series, specific PA/RFA)? Provide FOA number and any page or budget limits.

extra.2.question: Which proposal components are already complete and which are missing? (List specific aims, research strategy, budget & justification, biosketches, human subjects/IRB documents, data management plan, letters of support, abstract/summary).

extra.3.question: Do you expect human-subjects or protected-data issues (PHI, HIPAA)? If yes, is an IRB application already submitted and what is the expected approval timeline?
extra.3.value: expect human subjects but no protected data issues. irb is pending

extra.4.question: What is the status of preliminary data and analytic code? Are datasets available and documented, or do you need time to collect/clean data?

extra.5.question: Who will write/submit the budget and institutional budget justification? Are institutional rate agreements and salary/effort approvals available?
extra.5.value: my grand manager will deal with all of this

extra.6.question: How many letter writers / collaborators must provide signed letters of support, and have they agreed to deliver by specified dates? Provide names and expected delivery dates if known.
extra.6.value: need to identifu the writers and convince collaborators

hard_deadline.question: Is the external NIH/NIMH submission deadline February 15, 2026 absolute for this application? List any earlier internal institutional deadlines (e.g., departmental sign-off, grants office routing, eRA Commons approvals) and their dates. If any parts must be finished earlier than Feb 15 (e.g., letters of support, institutional approvals), specify dates.

key_constraints.question: What key constraints could prevent meeting the deadline? For each constraint below, state current status and an estimated completion date: IRB/IACUC approvals or human-subjects documentation; availability of co-investigators/collaborators and letter writers; institutional routing/signature requirements; budget ceiling or sponsor-imposed limits and indirect cost rate; page limits or format restrictions; access to preliminary data, datasets, core facilities; competing responsibilities (teaching/clinical duties) that reduce your available hours.
key_constraints.value: availability of co investigators, access to preliminary data

time_per_week_hours.question: How many hours per week can you personally commit, on average, to drafting and coordinating this NIMH proposal between now and submission? Please give a single number (e.g., 5, 10, 20).

risks: Overcommitment (plan doesn't fit weekly time budget)

forcing_questions: Which specific NIMH funding announcement or activity code (e.g., R01, R21, K-series, PA/FOA number) are you targeting?
What is the central research topic and proposed specific aims (even draft statements) for the application?
Who will be the PI and who are the key collaborators or co-investigators?
Do you have a current draft of any sections (specific aims, research strategy, budget, preliminary data)? If so, which?
What is the anticipated total budget or institutional cap, and are there constraints on personnel or indirect costs?
Will the project involve human subjects, vertebrate animals, or other regulated materials requiring IRB/IACUC/IBC approvals? If so, what is the current approval status?
Do you have institutional support letters and departmental approvals available or contacts to obtain them?
What is your timeline and available bandwidth for drafting, revising, and internal review prior to submission?
Are there required templates, formatting constraints, or submission portals (e.g., Grants.gov/eRA Commons) you already use or need help with?
Do you have preliminary data, datasets, or code that must be summarized or archived (data management plan)?
Who will handle budget preparation and institutional routing/submission processes?
Are there specific reviewers, themes, or NIMH priority areas you want the application to emphasize?

metric.method: Count required proposal components (e.g., specific aims, research strategy, budget and justification, biosketches, human subjects/IRB documentation, data management plan, letters of support, abstracts) and calculate the percentage that are finalized to submission-ready quality according to an NIMH checklist.
metric.name: Proposal completion percentage

smr.rationale: Securing NIMH funding will enable the proposed mental health research, support personnel and resources, and advance scientific understanding and interventions in a prioritized area of need.

goal.v1.text: Draft a complete grant proposal to the National Institute of Mental Health for external submission by February 15, 2026, and ready the full application package for institutional routing and internal review prior to that date.
